note: The spoken word carries no figure. A turn that points at a number sets "holds", and the page shows that figure live while the turn plays — so the audio never goes stale and the number is always the record as it stands.

turns.text: [shouting over engine noise] Gold Coast! [fast, excited] Surfers Paradise — and THAT is the Coates twenty-six. [driving, urgent] Before the crowds, before the flag, there's a build to deliver. [building to a shout] And today — the crew who deliver it get their moment!

[enthusiastic, jumping in] And haven't they earned it. [quick, rattling through] Buildings, toilets, access stairs, fencing, deliveries — every one with a place in the plan. [warm, landing it] And every one needs somebody who knows the job, looks after their mates, and sees it through.

[crisp, naming them like a grid] Andrew Fisher leads the Coates effort on site. [punchy, one at a time] Aaron Zelvis. Alfie Harris. Kyle Gover. [driving] Remember those names as we go round. [landing hard] This one belongs to the team behind the build.

[settling in, conversational] It starts with the pre-start. [quick, ticking off] Which load's coming? Where's it going? Who's spotting? What's changed since the plan? [warm] Everybody gets a say before the first move.

[driving] Race day is the deadline. [fast] The branch turns that into a schedule — the crew turn the schedule into work on the ground. [building] And when a delivery changes, or the next task wants a different approach, [landing hard] it's the talking that keeps it moving.

[firm, slowing right down] Safety and wellbeing come first. [measured] Check the space. Agree the signals. Look after the person beside you. [warm, deliberate] If something needs another look — give it another look. Knowing when to stop is part of being good at this.
[brisk, summing up] A clear plan. A crew who get it. People ready to listen. [landing] That's a strong way to start a day.

[driving] Aaron, Alfie and Kyle take on the work that looks easy once it's done. [slowing] Stand beside a building that's in position and level, stairs set — [landing] and you don't see a single decision it took to get there.

[quick, building] You see them on the way in. A tight approach. A careful walk round. Clearances checked, the driver guided, one controlled movement at a time. [wry] Andrew talks about spaces where you'd look at the truck and wonder how it could possibly fit. [warm] They work the plan. They make the move when it's right.

[fast] Then the set-up. [punchy, listing] Ground that shifts under you. Levels. Stairs. Access. The forklift, the spotting, the hands you need to keep it moving. [landing hard] That's the installation team's day — and it is a long way from dropping a load.

[warm, sincere] Their judgement matters. Their communication matters. [deliberate] So does the pride they take in the finish. [landing] There's a world of difference between arriving at a spot and handing over something properly set up for the people who'll use it.
[crisp, naming them] Aaron Zelvis. Alfie Harris. Kyle Gover. [building] Next time you walk past one of those buildings ready for use — [landing hard] remember the hands that put it there.
[crisp] And here's the count as it stands. [deliberate] Delivered, and installed — read separately, because they are not the same job. [landing] The record says which is which.
[driving] And this one stretches right across the site. [fast] Wayne Woods leads the Advanced Temporary Fencing crew — reading the drawings, working the sections that have to be ready.

[quick, rattling through] Panels, feet, clamps, gates, and the runs between them. [steady] The map gives them the references. The schedule gives them the order. [warm, landing] On the ground it's carrying, placing, connecting, checking. Section after section.
[driving] And there's where those metres stand right now. [landing hard] Every one of them carried, placed and checked by Wayne's crew.
[firm] Those metres are people. [crisp, naming them] Alongside Wayne — Owen Cowell McPaul. Daniel Macleod. Cody Woods. Chase Hireni. Tahi Peni. Daniel Smith. Scott Hildebrand.

[warm, insistent] Give every one of them the credit. [building] Drawings to follow, areas to work through, a programme running at race day. [landing hard] The fence is what everybody sees. Behind it is a crew who put in the hard yards to get it there.

[driving] Andrew's job is keeping it all connected. [fast] The plan from the branch. The deliveries coming through. The people doing the installing. [landing] Good coordination gives the crew clear priorities — and gets their questions to whoever can answer them.

[steady, sincere] The people on the ground know what the ground is telling them. [deliberate] Listen to that. If an approach needs changing, work it through together. If the next load wants a better order, take it back into the plan. [warm] It travels both ways.

[crisp, naming them] Krystal Stephens coordinates transport. Corey Machado looks after the account. Ross Saxelby and Abraham Tibble are the office support behind the job at Kingston. [landing] Their work joins up with Andrew's on site and with the crews doing the build.

[warm] A clear handover helps the next person do their job. [wry] A question answered early saves a lot of sorting out later. [building, landing hard] That's where the Coates Way gets practical. Make the work easier for each other. Keep the customer in mind. Do what you said you'd do.

[lighter, amused] And then there's McIntosh Island. [wry] Andrew reckons the birds are on just about everything. Roofs. Fences. The spot you're about to work in. [grinning] A few feathered supervisors, watching very closely.

[laughing] Especially when the food comes out. [warm] Smoko, barbecue on, the crew having a feed together. [sincere] There's room for a laugh in a busy job. It's part of what makes a team worth being in.

[serious now, slowing] Andrew's described thirty-degree days — and times it pushes towards forty. [deliberate] Water. Shade. Breaks. Looking after each other. [lighter] Coffee and slushies in the office don't go astray either.

[sincere, unhurried] People do demanding work here. [deliberate] Knowing they're supported. Knowing the effort's noticed. Being able to speak up. [landing] You want everyone finishing the day knowing they contributed — and that their mates had their back.

[punchy, one at a time] Care Deeply. Customer Focused. Be Our Best. One Team. Competitive Spirit. [driving] Those are the Coates values — [landing hard] and this build gives the people here a chance to put them to work every single day.

[warm, building] You see them in a careful move. A clear instruction. Someone taking responsibility. A mate offering a hand. [steady] In listening to a better idea. In doing the next bit properly. [landing] In giving the customer the gear and the support the job actually needs.

[proud] And there's plenty of pride in that. [crisp] Andrew Fisher and the branch behind him. Aaron, Alfie and Kyle on installation. Wayne and the fencing crew. [landing] And everyone helping each part of the plan come together.
[quick] Buildings. Amenities. Stairs. Fence lines. Gates. [steady, landing] The record tells you where the work stands. The people tell you how it got done.

[building, full voice] This is Coates Industrial Solutions at GC five hundred. [driving] A team putting in the hard yards, looking after one another, building towards race day. [landing hard] There's a bit of that team in every part of this place.
[sincere, very slow, quiet — let each phrase settle before the next] And every one of them... deserves... to be recognised.
[lifting again, into the engine] Stay with us. [fast] Another run with the Coates twenty-six — and another look at the people behind the roar!

[energetic, returning] Back with the Coates twenty-six on the Gold Coast! [fast] Just joining us — this is the crew putting the GC five hundred build together, with Andrew Fisher leading the Coates effort on site.

[quick, warm] The branch planning. The installers on the ground. Wayne's fencing team. [landing] A lot of different work, joined up by people who care about getting it right. [driving] Let's take you through it.
